subject: Genetics
title: What Three Billion Letters Look Like
description: Learn What Three Billion Letters Look Like in one minute.

hook.text: If you printed the human genome in books, it would fill 200 volumes of 1,000 pages each. Just four letters: A, T, C, G.

buildup.text: Those letters pair predictably: A with T, C with G. The pairing holds the double helix together like a zipper.

discovery.text: The order of letters determines everything: eye color, disease risk, how your brain develops. Sequence is destiny.

twist.text: Two humans differ in only 0.1% of their genome—about 3 million letters. Tiny changes create all human diversity.

climax.text: Reading those letters was step one. Understanding what they mean is step two—and we're still working on it.

punchline.text: The book is written. We're still learning to read.

quiz.question: How much do two humans differ in their DNA?
